chapter: Clarinetists, brass bands and the day job
title: Letter carrier in 1919 and earnings at the roofing trade
summary: He carried mail for eighteen months, quit in 1919 for the roofing trade, whose pay rose far past the post office's, and he now owns rental property.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Oh, I thought that was right.

I gave it up. Went back to my trade. In 1919. I scanned mail in 1919. I gave it up. So, I gave 18 months carrying mail and I gave it up. Went back to my trade, which I was doing. So, I was in the post office making 3,020 cents a day. I just raised our salary to $6 a day. You understand? So, I went back to my trade. So, the knife supervisor, Mr. Fogarty, I was in the post office making 3,020 cents a day. I just raised our salary to $6 a day. You understand? So, I went back to my trade. So, the knife supervisor, Mr. Freyley told me, he says, August, I don't blame you. He said, I ain't making that. He said, I jump up to grab that job right now. So, I went back to my trade. Next two, three months, I was making eight. Next two, three months, I was making 10. Then another fella got rushed with some work. He offered me 12. I got released from my boss and I told him, I said, I'm going to give Jerry the Brothers a hand. He gave me $12 a day to work for me. Well, I was pretty fast working and good work. I knew the works. Well, he gave me $12 a day and went on like that. And told my salary got up to $30 a day. You know? To stop, I had to stop. Stop altogether. I'm not doing nothing. All the work I do now is part of it for myself. I got a couple of little places running out, you know, apartments. Steady income. That big house I'll just show you there. I'll show you the pictures of them. Point Street and all. It was fourplex.
Well, you still have the house up there on Fairmont.
I get $85 a size. Upstairs, $65 for downstairs.
